drivingQuestion: What does 'one who makes his prayer keva' mean in R' Eliezer's mishna?
outcomeNote: Three definitions of keva are offered side by side and none is chosen; the series of definitions continues in the next unit (berakhot.sugya237).

segments.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר כׇּל הָעוֹשֶׂה תְּפִלָּתוֹ קֶבַע וְכוּ׳: מַאי ״קֶבַע״? אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא: כֹּל שֶׁתְּפִלָּתוֹ דּוֹמָה עָלָיו כְּמַשּׂוֹי. וְרַבָּנַן אָמְרִי: כׇּל מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ אוֹמְרָהּ בִּלְשׁוֹן תַּחֲנוּנִים. רַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף דְאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ: כֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְחַדֵּשׁ בָּהּ דָּבָר.
segments.en: We learned in the mishna that «Rabbi Eliezer says: One whose prayer is fixed, his prayer is not supplication.» The Gemara asks: «What is» the meaning of «fixed» in this context? «Rabbi Ya’akov bar Idi said» that «Rabbi Oshaya said:» It means «anyone for whom his prayer is like a burden upon him,» from which he seeks to be quickly unburdened. «The Rabbis say:» This refers to «anyone who does not recite» prayer «in the language of supplication,» but as a standardized recitation without emotion. «Rabba and Rav Yosef both said:» It refers to «anyone unable to introduce» a novel «element,» i.e., something personal reflecting his personal needs, to his prayer, and only recites the standard formula.
